<!-- Guidance for the author. Delete these comments before submitting; they stay in
the text even though the page hides them.
- Keep Outcome and context and Acceptance criteria; delete any other section,
  heading included, that would add nothing.
- Make the issue understandable on its own. Say each thing once; if it fits several
  sections, choose one.
- Say what you observed, what was reported (and by whom) and what you assume; mark
  anything without evidence as unverified. Do not invent missing details.
- Give file paths you have confirmed; mark a guess as a guess.
- Label suggestions and proposals as such and say whose they are. Mark a criterion
  that is your own addition, not an agreed requirement, as proposed.
- Put undecided points under open questions, not among the requirements.
- Aim for one reviewable pull request per repository; use an epic when the outcome
  needs coordination across several issues.
- Use the names found in the code or product, and summarize any source the reader
  cannot open. -->

## Outcome and context
<!-- What needs to change, and why? What happens today? -->

## Scope and constraints
<!-- What is out of scope, agreed constraints, and decisions or options already
ruled out. -->

## Starting points
<!-- Relevant code, patterns, designs or examples, and what the work relies on
from each. -->

## Acceptance criteria
<!-- Observable results that complete this change, as `- [ ]` items. Include
existing behavior that must keep working. -->

## How to verify
<!-- Checks specific to this change. Delete this section if the acceptance criteria
already say how each result is checked. -->

## Dependencies and open questions
<!-- Parent epic and blocking issues (also set as GitHub relationships), and
unanswered questions with what each one blocks. -->
